title: Code verification: hidden tests, new processes, gVisor, no network, and test strength
design_ref: Code verification: tests that are hard to fool
purpose: Look at where the code verifiers run and what they can reach, send the strict one programs that try to cheat in ways its static scan does not see, and measure how strong each task's hidden tests are by mutation testing.

checks.description: the strict code verifier runs in gVisor's user-space kernel; the old one on the node's own kernel
checks.because: runtimeClassName: gvisor puts the pod on the sandbox node and starts it with runsc.

checks.description: the verifier pod cannot reach the internet
checks.because: The rewards NetworkPolicy allows only DNS, the store, the judges and its own namespace.

checks.description: reading the hidden tests without the word 'open' is still refused, by the audit hook in the child process
checks.because: The static scan misses io.FileIO; the harness's audit hook raises on any open outside the scratch directory and the stdlib.

checks.description: an endless loop, a 2 GB allocation and a fork all fail; the correct program passes
checks.because: Each test runs in a new process with 4 s of CPU, 512 MB of address space and a 10 s wall clock; the audit hook refuses os.fork.

checks.description: mutation testing flags the two tasks with thin tests and admits the rest (threshold 0.85)
checks.because: A mutant of the reference solution that passes every hidden test shows a hole in the tests, not in the verifier.
